I farm 16.1 mu with only two people in the household, so I will keep the plan simple and stable. I have 40 years of experience, and at my age I care more about reliable output and manageable labor than taking risks. Since I have well irrigation and my main system is wheat-maize, I will keep most of the land in that rotation because it fits my habits, machinery, and water conditions. I will leave 4.1 mu for cotton because I already grow it and it helps spread risk across crops and market prices. For seed, I will use improved seed for wheat, hybrid seed for maize, and improved seed for cotton, because I want steady emergence, stronger resistance, and better yield potential without making the management too complicated. For fertilizer, I will keep inputs at moderate levels: enough to support yield, but not excessive, because overuse raises cost and can lodge wheat or push maize too hard. With well irrigation, I will irrigate wheat more times since it needs water at key stages, maize fewer times because summer rain helps, and cotton a moderate number of times for stability. I will use rotary tillage on the wheat-maize land because it is efficient for me, and plough the cotton land to loosen soil more deeply. I will control pests with a moderate number of sprays, especially in cotton, because cotton is more vulnerable and needs closer watching. Overall, I will aim for a balanced plan that matches my labor, my land, and what has worked for me over the years.
